title: Decoding Immune Predictors of Response to Immunotherapy via Multiomics Analysis
author: Jian, Zheng, et al.

steps.title: Recruit patients and apply criteria
steps.instruction: Select patients according to the study’s inclusion criteria (histopathological cancer confirmation, completion of therapy per protocol, clinical suitability for biopsy, adequate organ function and life expectancy) and exclude any receiving concurrent therapies (chemotherapy, targeted agents, immunomodulators), enrolled in other interventional trials, or with study‑specific exclusion reasons (pharmacokinetic interactions, overlapping toxicities, compromised response assessment).

steps.title: Prepare computing hardware
steps.instruction: Ensure access to a high‑performance computing cluster or workstation with sufficient RAM and storage to handle large‑scale single‑cell sequencing data.

steps.title: Install R and required packages
steps.instruction: Install R ≥ 4.2.1 and RStudio, then install the following packages (versions as listed): Seurat 4.2.1, ComplexHeatmap, AUCell, scFunctions, rcartocolor, Monocle 2, Liana, and any additional packages for visualization and statistics. Verify installation before proceeding.

steps.title: Set up data management
steps.instruction: Create a secure, organized directory structure for raw and processed data, enable regular backups, and use a version‑control system (e.g., Git) for analysis scripts.

steps.title: Process raw scRNA‑seq data
steps.instruction: Run CellRanger v6.1.0 on raw FASTQ files using the GRCh38 reference to demultiplex, align, and quantify reads.

substeps.instruction: Command: cellranger count --id=sample --transcriptome=GRCh38 --fastqs=path_to_fastqs
Collect the resulting gene‑cell matrix for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Quality control and doublet removal
steps.instruction: Filter cells based on gene count, mitochondrial content, and doublet score, then retain the filtered matrix.

substeps.instruction: Remove cells with < 6000 detected genes (adjustable based on sequencing depth).
Remove cells with > 30 % mitochondrial gene counts (use 10‑25 % for healthy PBMCs, up to 30‑40 % for stressed tissue).
Detect doublets with DoubletFinder using BCMVN‑optimized pK selection; discard identified doublets.
Proceed with the remaining gene‑cell matrix.

steps.title: Normalize and select variable genes
steps.instruction: Normalize counts with Seurat v4.2.1 (scale factor = 10,000), log‑transform, center and scale, then select the top 2000 highly variable genes (HVGs).

substeps.instruction: NormalizeData(object, scale.factor = 10000)
FindVariableFeatures(object, selection.method = "vst", nfeatures = 2000)

steps.title: Dimensionality reduction and batch integration
steps.instruction: Perform PCA on the HVGs, integrate batches with Harmony v0.1.1 on the top 30 PCs, then compute UMAP on the first 30 Harmony embeddings.

substeps.instruction: RunPCA(object, features = VariableFeatures(object), npcs = 30)
RunHarmony(object, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:30)
RunUMAP(object, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:30)

steps.title: Construct SNN graph and cluster cells
steps.instruction: Build a shared‑nearest‑neighbor (SNN) graph using Jaccard index with k = 20 nearest neighbors and cluster via modularity optimization.

substeps.instruction: FindNeighbors(object, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:30, k.param = 20, method = "jaccard")
FindClusters(object, resolution = appropriate_value)

steps.title: Separate CD4 and CD8 T‑cell subsets and plot UMAPs
steps.instruction: Load the integrated Seurat object, split into CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ subsets, and generate PDF UMAP plots of cell‑type composition for each subset (width = 10 in, height = 8 in).

substeps.instruction: cd4 <- subset(seurat_obj, idents = "CD4")
cd8 <- subset(seurat_obj, idents = "CD8")
pdf("UMAP_CD4_CD8_Cell_Types.pdf", width=10, height=8)
DimPlot(cd4, group.by = "Cell_Type")
DimPlot(cd8, group.by = "Cell_Type")
dev.off()

steps.title: Identify cluster‑defining marker genes
steps.instruction: For each CD4 or CD8 cluster, locate differentially expressed genes (DEGs) by comparing the cluster against all other cells; store average expression matrices in a list named `allave`.

substeps.instruction: Iterate over DEG result files, assign identities with Idents(), and save average expression matrices to `allave`.

steps.title: Generate heatmap of DEGs
steps.instruction: Create a PDF heatmap (width = 6 in, height = 4 in) of the DEG expression matrix, splitting columns by treatment (Pre vs Post) and cell type (CD4 vs CD8), using a reversed RdYlBu palette (100 colors) and annotating treatment and cell‑type classes.

substeps.instruction: Prepare HeatmapAnnotation for treatment and cell‑type.
Heatmap(plotx, column_split = csplit, top_annotation = ca, col = cols, ...)
pdf(...); print(Heatmap(...)); dev.off()

steps.title: Create dot plots for marker genes
steps.instruction: Produce PDF dot plots (width = 10 in, height = 14 in) of signature markers for CD4 and CD8 subsets, using a blue‑yellow‑red gradient, scaled point size (1–6), and a clean theme.

substeps.instruction: Loop over marker gene sets, generate ggplot objects with geom_dotplot, apply scale_color_gradientn, scale_size, theme settings, and save to PDF.

steps.title: Plot stacked barplots of cell‑type proportions
steps.instruction: Generate a PDF stacked barplot (width = 14 in, height = 6 in) showing proportional changes of `Cell_Type` across cancer types, faceted by `IIID` group, using a custom color palette `ccols` and placing the legend at the bottom.

substeps.instruction: Remove previous object `x` with rm(x).
Load pre‑calculated proportions into `prop`.
ggplot(prop, aes(Cancer, Proportion, fill = Cell_Type)) + geom_bar(position = "stack", stat = "identity") + facet_wrap(~IIID, ncol = 4) + ... + dev.off()

steps.title: Analyze regulon activity and plot phylogenetic tree
steps.instruction: Load pre‑computed regulon AUC scores, compute correlation‑based distances, construct a phylogenetic tree, and output PDF plots (width = 14 in, height = 14 in) with tip labels colored by cancer type and shaped by cell type.

substeps.instruction: rm(x); load regulon AUC data into `allaucs`.
For each treatment group, create a matrix `mplotx` of AUC values.
Compute distance matrix with `dist()` on correlation, build tree with `hclust()` or `ape::nj()`, plot with ggplot2, add `geom_tiplab`, `scale_color_manual(cancercols)`, `scale_shape_manual`.
Save each plot to PDF.

steps.title: Visualize TCR clonal expansion (scatter plots)
steps.instruction: Load TCR clonal expansion statistics and create two PDF scatter plots (width = 12 in, height = 6 in): one colored by `FC_Group` and another by `Clonal_log2FC_G2vsG1`, both sized by significance level, then save both plots to a single PDF.

substeps.instruction: pdf("Clonal_Homeostasis_Post_RNR_Specific_TBCRs.pdf", width=12, height=6)
ggplot(tcrdata, aes(Cell_Type, Cancer, color = FC_Group, size = Sig_Level)) + geom_point() + labs(title = "Post(R) vs Post(NR)") + theme_classic() + RotatedAxis()
ggplot(tcrdata, aes(Cell_Type, Cancer, color = Clonal_log2FC_G2vsG1, size = Sig_Level)) + geom_point() + labs(title = "Post(R) vs Post(NR)") + theme_classic() + RotatedAxis()
dev.off()

steps.title: Boxplot analysis of TCR clonal frequency
steps.instruction: Define comparison groups, generate per‑cell‑type boxplots with statistical annotations (t‑test and Wilcoxon), combine them into a multi‑panel figure (width = 8 in, height = 8 in), and save as PDF.

substeps.instruction: Load TCR data, set `ccompare` and `selected` cell types.

For each cell type, create a ggplot boxplot with `geom_boxplot(alpha = 0)`, `geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge())`, `stat_compare_means(method = "t.test")` and `stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test")`.
Combine plots with `combine_plots(..., nrow = 2)` and add a unified title.
pdf("FigurexxxxA2_Boxplot_Expansion0_Clonal_Homeostasis_Post_RNR_Specific_TBCRs.pdf", width=8, height=8); print(combined_plot); dev.off()

steps.title: Perform cell‑cell interaction analysis with LIANA
steps.instruction: Load the `liana` package, read all interaction result files, rename source/target labels (e.g., replace "Responder_Post_RvsNR" with "Post_R"), save each processed object as an RDS file, then plot the top 20 significant interactions (FDR < 0.01) per sender cell type in a PDF (width = 20 in, height = 8 in).

substeps.instruction: library(liana); files <- list.files(pattern = "\.rds$")
for each file: load, clean labels with gsub, saveRDS(...).
pdf(paste0("CellCell_",cname,"_Top_20_Interactions.pdf"), width=20, height=8)

For each sender cell type `cts[k]`, if interactions exist, plot with `geom_point` (size, color gradient), `RotatedAxis()`, custom theme, `scale_color_gradientn(color_conditions$gradient)`, and `ggtitle(paste("CRC: ",cname))`.
dev.off()

steps.title: Build response prediction model (RI)
steps.instruction: Conduct differential expression between responders and non‑responders for each IRAT cell type and cancer, compute composite GSEA indices (TS and TP groups), calculate composite clonal fold‑change index, and derive the Response Index (RI) as the product of GSEA and clonal FC indices using elastic‑net regression (glmnet α = 0.3) with caret for model training.

substeps.instruction: DE analysis: Wilcoxon Rank‑Sum test with Bonferroni adjustment; select genes with ≥ 50 % votes for “Responder”.
GSEA: Use MSigDB gene sets to obtain TS (CD4/CXCL13+ Tfh, CD8/CXCL13+ T) and TP (CD4/TGFβ1+ T, CD8 Temra) scores; sum to get composite GSEA index.
Clonal FC index: absolute sum of TS clonal FC divided by sum of TP indices.
RI = composite GSEA index × composite clonal FC index.
Train elastic‑net model with glmnet (α = 0.3) via caret, evaluate performance, and output model, indices, and RI thresholds.

steps.title: Survival analysis using bulk RNA‑seq
steps.instruction: Collect four post‑ICB bulk RNA‑seq cohorts (IMvigor210, Liu2019 SKCM, Riaz2017 SKCM, Braun2020 ccRCC), extract IRAT signature expression (e.g., CXCL13, TGFβ1), stratify patients into high/low groups using maximally selected rank statistics (MSRS) between the 10‑th and 90‑th percentiles, compute CXCL13/TGFβ1 ratio, optionally stratify by tumor mutational burden (TMB) if available, then perform Kaplan‑Meier survival curves and log‑rank tests, and fit Cox proportional‑hazards models to report hazard ratios with confidence intervals.

substeps.instruction: Load each bulk dataset, subset to signature genes.
Apply `maxstat::maxstat.test` to determine optimal cut‑points for high vs low expression.
Create survival objects with `survfit` and plot curves.
Use `survdiff` for log‑rank p‑values.
Fit `coxph` models for each marker and report HR and 95 % CI.

description: The primary scientific objective of this protocol is to characterize the factors influencing immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) response across multiple cancer types. This protocol will identify T cell subsets that correlate with ICB response and resistance by analyzing T cell dynamics using single-cell RNA sequencing and mass cytometry (CyTOF). We will perform gene regulatory network analysis to identify clinically relevant transcription factors and their associated regulatory networks. Cell-cell interaction analysis will systematically map interactions between T cells and neighboring immune cells to explore immune signaling. T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire analysis will examine clonal expansion patterns associated with ICB response. Finally, we will integrate these data to construct a response prediction model that can identify patients likely to respond to ICB therapy. Additionally, this protocol can be applied to identify new biomarkers for other diseases, guide the development of new immunotherapies or combination therapies, design and monitor clinical trials, and address fundamental research questions in immunology and cancer biology. The comprehensive single-cell multiomics approach provides a versatile framework for uncovering new biological mechanisms and pathways, enhancing its utility and impact across various research and clinical applications.2
